# Alternative Models (Online Only) {.appendix #sec-appendix-alt-models}


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
library(modelsummary)

here::here("code", "formatting.R") |> source()
```


## Alternative Specifications 

For three types of results, we used modified versions of @eq-full. We estimate additional models as robustness checks. 

### Majority Status 

Because committee leadership positions depend on chair status, we omitted majority status when estimating chair effects. To estimate the effects of majority status on interbranch work we added a majority status indicator to @eq-full. We also estimated modified models with majority status but without committee leadership variables. 
Each section includes a model where we exclude committee leadership positions that depend on majority status, in order to estimate the effect of majority status among all members (not just those without leadership positions, who are structurally more likely to be in the minority, or junior members of the majority). 


### PAC Contributions 

Because fundraising is also closely tied to committee positions as both a cause of appointment to chair positions and an effect of leadership positions, we did not include PAC fundraising in the main specification to estimate committee leadership effects. To estimate relationships with PAC contributions, we estimated separate models, identical to  @eq-full, but adding PAC contributions.

### Right Wing and Left Wing 

Our main specification estimates the relationship between political party and interbranch representation, controlling for the absolute value of 1st Dimension DW-NOMINATE scores. To estimate difference in interbranch representation done by the right wing, we estimate modified models where we substitute a "right wing" (NOMINATE scores greater than 0.5) indicator for the party indicator and the absolute value of 1st Dimension DW-NOMINATE scores. Finally, to compare right wing legislators to moderates, we added a control for "left wing" (NOMINATE scores less than -0.5). These alternative models are available online in @sec-appendix-e-alt-models, along with other models estimated as robustest checks. 

### Robustness Checks 

The main specification used a combined modeling approach.  Here we separate the parts of our framework and test the effects of constituent demand, capacity, and the Incentives on interbranch representation separately, without adjusting for effects of the other parts. This alternative specification may be informative if we believe that parts are causally related (for example, if people from large states are more likely to become committee chairs or if more moderate members are more likely to face competitive general elections), or if some variables may be co-linear.


#### Modeling Response to Constituency Demands

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_{ijt}\mid X_{ijt},\gamma_{ij},\delta_{jt},m_{it},p_{it} &\sim \text{NegBin}(\mu_{ijt},\alpha), \\
\log(\mu_{ijt}) = 
  & \beta_1 \text{District Population}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_2 \text{Percent Goverment Workers}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_3 \text{Percent with College Degree}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_4 \text{Percent Receiving Public Assistance}_{it}+\\
  &...\\
  & \gamma_{ij} + \delta_{jt} 
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-demand}


#### Modeling Capacity Effects


$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_{ijt}\mid X_{ijt},\gamma_{ij},\delta_{jt},m_{it},p_{it} &\sim \text{NegBin}(\mu_{ijt},\alpha), \\
\log(\mu_{ijt}) = 
  & \beta_1 \text{Experience in Office}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_2 \text{Experience as State Legislator}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_3 \text{Staff Budget}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_4 \text{Oversight Committee Position}_{itj}+\\
  & \beta_5 \text{Committee Chair}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_6 \text{Subcommittee Chair}_{it}+\\
  & \beta_7 \text{Ranking Minority Committee Member}_{it}+\\
  &...\\
  & \gamma_{ij} + \delta_{jt} 
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-capacity}

```{r}
type = "total"
```


### Majority Status 

::: {.fake-xref-table-for-caption}

```{=latex}

```

|   |
|---|
|   |

: The effect of Constituent Demand, Legislator Capacity, and Incentives (including majority status) on non-profit/local government service {#tbl-models-full-majority-non}

```{=latex}

```
:::

```{r}
load(here::here("models", type,  "models_full_majority.Rdata"))

modelsummary(models_full_majority,
             notes = list(
               "Robust standard errors in parentheses, clustered by legislator.",
               "This table shows estimates of The effect of Constituent Demand, Legislator Capacity and Incentives on levels of interbranch representation.")) |>
  # get rid of formatting to get rid of the extra line 
  theme_empty() |> 
  # bold header, hline bottom, aligned center
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 0:1, bold = T, line = "b",  align = "c") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 1, align = "l")  |>  
  # new stuff for this table 
  tinytable::theme_latex(multipage = TRUE) |> 
  group_tt(i = list(
    "Constituent Demand"= 2,
    "Incentives Shaped by Incentives" = 10,
    "Capacity" = 28
  )) |>
  style_tt(i = 39, line = "t", line_color = "black", line_width = 0.1) |>
  style_tt("groupi", background = "grey") |>
  style_tt("~groupi", j = 1, indent = 1)
```
